title: 7 Stocks to Buy When the AI Bubble Turns 2000
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue argues the AI sell-off in CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle echoes the dot-com bust: the whole buildout rests on OpenAI and Anthropic revenue that public investors cannot yet audit, and he expects the real break three to six months after Anthropic's IPO, when several quarters of results are visible. Like Amazon after 2000, he says the winners will be companies using AI rather than building infrastructure, and he is buying seven of them slowly — a little now, more every month or two, while holding cash back for a crash. The seven are UiPath, ServiceNow, Palantir, Cloudflare, SoundHound AI, Tempus AI (captions say 'Tempest AI') and Snowflake, each assessed on operating and free cash flow, balance-sheet cash and survivability if financing dries up, with analyst targets shown for context. Palantir is the exception on timing: he wants $150–$160 before loading up. Calls: PATH — BUY (first tracked, average target $15.57); NOW — BUY (flip from UNCERTAIN, target $155 as stated in captions, a figure that looks garbled); PLTR — CONDITIONAL_BUY (flip from BUY, buy zone $150–$160); NET — BUY (flip from UNCERTAIN, target $358); SOUN — BUY (flip from HOLD, target $11); TEM — BUY (first tracked, target $73); SNOW — BUY (first tracked, target $438).

calls.thesis: First tracked Hogue PATH call, in his seven stocks to buy for the post-AI-bubble world (staged buying: a little now, add every month or two, keep cash for a crash): UiPath is moving from repetitive-task automation into AI agents that interpret information and complete workflows, without spending billions on models or data centres; already $370M+ operating cash flow, $360M+ free cash flow and $619M cash, so it can survive a financing dry-up; risk is its original automation being made obsolete by Microsoft/OpenAI-type competitors.
calls.price_at_call: Down ~18% over the last year; analyst average target $15.57 (~20% upside) as stated

calls.thesis: ServiceNow as the orchestration layer between a company's AI agents and AI models, routing agents to the most efficient model and controlling AI costs; revenue expected up 22% this year, $5.3B operating cash flow and $4.5B+ free cash flow, $2.5B cash — no survivability worry; risk is Microsoft, Salesforce and AI developers competing in the same orchestration role; he thinks Wall Street is too focused on software risks and the stock goes much higher.
calls.price_at_call: Down ~21% over 12 months; analyst average target $155 (~10% upside) as stated in captions — that target figure looks garbled, treat with caution

calls.thesis: Palantir could be one of the biggest winners from turning AI into real-world business decisions (revenue expected up 83% this year, ~50% next year; $3.4B operating/free cash flow, $2B+ cash), but valuation is the big risk at 163x earnings / 80x sales — he wants it down to around $160 or even $150 a share before jumping in too much and is not loading up at the current price.
calls.price_at_call: His buy zone $150-$160; analyst average target $212 (~13% upside), low target $80 (-57%) as stated

calls.thesis: Cloudflare as the management/secure layer between AI agents and models, with authentication and protection built in, on top of its global security/connectivity network; revenue expected up 32% this year and profits up 35% to $1.26/share, $633M operating cash flow and ~$1.7B cash — enough to survive an AI crash and ramp back up.
calls.price_at_call: Up ~38% over 12 months; analyst average target $358 (~21% upside), low target $160 as stated

calls.thesis: SoundHound in his seven to buy for the post-bubble world despite being one of the riskiest names: voice AI for restaurants, customer service and autos, a stated $140B market opportunity, revenue expected up 73% this year to almost $300M and 32% next year — but it has never generated positive cash flow and depends on constant financing (~$200M cash on hand as stated); he first recommended it near $4.80 in early 2024, had shares called away around $15 in January and bought back just under $9 in April.
calls.price_at_call: Analyst average target $11 (more than double the current price as stated); low target $6 (~26% upside)

calls.thesis: First tracked Hogue TEM call (captions say 'Tempest AI' for Tempus AI): combines clinical records, genomic information and AI to help doctors choose treatments; its growing clinical/genomic library could be hard to replicate; revenue expected up 25% this year and the earnings loss narrowing to ~5c/share next year — but it burns ~$270M cash a year ($600M+ cash on hand) and faces healthcare-regulation risk, so survivability is a question mark. He recommended it on 15 July.
calls.price_at_call: Down ~27% over the last year, up ~15% since his 15 July recommendation; analyst average target $73 (~10% upside) as stated

calls.thesis: First tracked Hogue SNOW call and one of his favourite growth stories: Snowflake helps companies organise and use proprietary data that AI agents need, with Cortex AI built directly on that data; revenue expected up 35% this year, $1.2B operating cash flow and nearly as much free cash flow, $1.7B cash and debt being paid down — no survivability worry.
calls.price_at_call: Up ~26% over 12 months, down ~20% from the peak in last week's sell-off; analyst average target $438 (~41% upside), low target $360 (~16% upside) as stated
